questions.title: Wildcard String Matching
questions.statement:
Given an input string **s** and a pattern **p**, implement wildcard pattern matching with support for \`?\` and \`*\`.

- \`?\` matches any single character.
- \`*\` matches any sequence of characters, including the empty sequence.

The match must cover the **entire** input string, not only a substring. Return \`true\` if \`p\` matches \`s\`; otherwise return \`false\`.
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains the string s.\nThe second line contains the pattern p.
questions.outputFormat: Print true if the entire string matches the pattern; otherwise print false.
questions.constraints: 0 <= s.length, p.length <= 2000\ns contains lowercase English letters only.\np contains lowercase English letters, ? or *.

questions.title: Rabin-Karp Algorithm for Pattern Searching
questions.statement:
Given two strings: a text string in which you want to search, and a pattern string that you are looking for within the text. Return all positions (0-based indexing) where the pattern occurs as a substring in the text. If the pattern does not occur, return an empty list.

![Rabin-Karp pattern matching example](/rabin-karp-pattern-search.png)

Use the Rabin-Karp rolling-hash technique. Verify matching hash windows character by character to avoid collisions.
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains the text string.\nThe second line contains the pattern string.
questions.outputFormat: Print the 0-based starting indices in the format [i, j, ...]. Print [] when there are no matches.
questions.constraints: 1 <= text.length <= 10^5\n1 <= pattern.length <= text.length\nBoth strings contain lowercase English letters.

questions.title: Word Wrap
questions.statement:
Given an array arr[], where arr[i] denotes the number of characters in one word. Let k be the limit on the number of characters that can be put in one line (line width). Put line breaks in the given sequence such that the lines are printed neatly.

Assume that the length of each word is smaller than the line width.

When line breaks are inserted there is a possibility that extra spaces are present in each line. The extra spaces include spaces put at the end of every line except the last one. You have to minimize the following total cost:

**Total Cost = Sum of cost of all lines**
**Cost of line = (Number of extra spaces in the line)²**

**Example 1:**
- Input: arr[] = [3,2,2,5], k = 6
- Output: 10
- Explanation: Line 1: From word 1 to 1 ("word of length 3") → extra spaces = 6 - 3 = 3 → cost = 3² = 9
Line 2: From word 2 to 3 ("words of length 2 and 2 with 1 space between") → extra spaces = 6 - 2 - 2 - 1 = 1 → cost = 1² = 1
Line 3: From word 4 to 4 (last line, no extra space cost) → cost = 0
Total cost = 9 + 1 + 0 = 10

**Example 2:**
- Input: arr[] = [3,2,2], k = 4
- Output: 5
- Explanation: Line 1: Word 1 → extra spaces = 4 - 3 = 1 → cost = 1² = 1
Line 2: Word 2 → extra spaces = 4 - 2 = 2 → cost = 2² = 4
Line 3: Word 3 (last line) → cost = 0
Total cost = 1 + 4 + 0 = 5
questions.inputFormat: First line contains n (number of words), second line contains n space-separated integers representing word lengths, third line contains k (line width limit).
questions.outputFormat: Return the minimum total cost to arrange the words optimally.
